about: Behaviour changes from the release notes, one entry per probed behaviour candidate (data/candidates/release_notes.json), not only the chosen concepts. old_gold and new_gold are the inventory symbols a concept on the change uses on each side; they may coincide. Entries count only when the probe found a direction (rules.behaviour_rules). These rules link gold pairs in validation step 7 and the doc-conflict test; they are never signals (user decision 2026-10-18).

rules.quote: numpy.floor, numpy.ceil, and numpy.trunc now won't perform casting to a floating dtype for integer and boolean dtype input arrays.
the unique_inverse output is now shaped such that the input can be reconstructed directly using np.take(unique, unique_inverse) when axis=None
Now a string of "0" will be considered True since it is not empty.
np.float32(3) + 3. now returns a float32 when it previously returned a float64.
the complex sign is now calculated as z / |z|
The any and all functions and methods now return booleans also for object arrays.
Conversion of an array with ndim > 0 to a scalar was deprecated in NumPy 1.25. Now, attempting to do so raises TypeError.
Functions that returned a list of ndarrays have been changed to return a tuple of ndarrays instead.
numpy.count_nonzero for axis=None (default) now returns a NumPy scalar instead of a Python integer.
The old behaviour can be reconstructed by using np.solve(a, b[..., None])[..., 0].
conversion of 255 to int8 will not return -1.
loadtxt and genfromtxt now both default to encoding=None which may mainly modify how converters work. These will now be passed str rather than bytes.
